claim_one_line: THE DICTIONARY ENTRY IS AN IDENTITY, AND THE ANSWER TO B8104'S QUESTION IS 'NONE OF THEM'. Third rung of the owner-elected finish-the-3d-theory line. B8104 closed with one named gap: does the AdS3 boundary-graviton one-loop determinant correspond to one of Pfaff's rho(m) torsions, and if so which? DEFINITIONS READ FROM THE SOURCE (arXiv:1206.0228) RATHER THAN RECALLED: rho(m) is the 2m-th symmetric power of the standard SL2(C) rep on Sym^{2m}C^2, dimension 2m+1; sigma_k is the representation of M = SO2(R) with highest weight k e_2 and is ONE-DIMENSIONAL; R(s,sigma) = prod over prime classes of det(Id - sigma(m_gamma) e^{-s l(gamma)}), absolutely convergent for Re(s) > 2. BECAUSE sigma_k IS ONE-DIMENSIONAL, sigma_k(m_gamma) = e^{i k theta_gamma}, so R(k,sigma_k) = prod_gamma (1 - q_gamma^k) with q_gamma = e^{-l + i theta} -- EXACTLY the Giombi-Maloney-Yin nome. Hence the graviton product is prod_{n>=2} |R(n,sigma_n)|^{-2}: an INFINITE product of one-dimensional Ruelle zetas, while every rho(m) torsion is a FINITE object, so no single one can be it. What Theorem 1.2 supplies is the TAIL, prod_{k=3}^{m}|R(k,sigma_k)| expressed as a torsion ratio times an explicit cusp defect and volume factor. VERIFIED NOT ASSERTED: re-summing B8100's own spectrum in the opposite order agrees to 8.2e-14 and reproduces its banked log Z_geod = -0.2729771708384 exactly. AND THE IDENTIFICATION EXPLAINS B8100'S ERROR BAR: R(s,sigma) converges absolutely for Re(s) > 2 and the graviton product STARTS AT n = 2, the boundary -- so all the cutoff instability should live in one factor, and it does: the last cutoff step moves the n=2 term by 1.95e-3 against 9.67e-6 for the entire n>=3 tail, a factor of 202, and the n=2 term is the one that changes sign. B8100 reported oscillatory convergence and quoted the last delta as an honest error; this says WHY -- the graviton's n=2 mode sits exactly at the abscissa of absolute convergence of the Ruelle zeta, which is ALSO why Pfaff's theorem starts at m >= 3 and normalises by rho(2). The structure of the physics and the structure of the theorem have the same boundary. WHAT THAT BUYS: with kappa(X) = 1 and vol(X) = 2.029883212819307, the analytic torsion ratio T_X(rho(m))/T_X(rho(2)) for the figure-eight knot complement is computed as 1.429269e-02 (m=3), 6.223622e-05 (m=4), 7.993938e-08 (m=5), 2.907261e-11 (m=6), with relative uncertainty 4.8e-6 from the k>=3 Ruelle product's cutoff stability, which is 420x better than the n=2 term -- precisely why the torsion ratio is quotable when the full one-loop is not. c(m) was RECOMPUTED WITH A SCRIPT, since B8104 banked its values with none, and the parenthesisation is DECLARED in the code because the source transcription is ambiguous; it reproduces B8104's numbers to ten decimals, so the two runs verify each other. A CONTROL DEFECT FOUND IN B8100, RESULT UNAFFECTED: its 'geodesics come in complex-conjugate pairs' gate ran on length_spectrum(2.0) while its headline used cutoff 5.5 -- the control was run on a DIFFERENT DATA SET than the result. Below 5.5 there are four self-conjugate classes at theta = pi (e^{i pi} = e^{-i pi}) that a naive pairing test rejects, and none appears below 2.0, so the control passed only where it was vacuous. B8100's number is unaffected and is reproduced here to 1e-13; this is a CONTROL defect, not a result defect, and is the frame-not-instance refinement of E2 recurring -- filed as an E2 instance, not a new class. My own first repair failed too: (theta1+theta2) mod 2pi returns ~2pi rather than ~0 for a sum a hair below 2pi, fixed to measure distance to the nearest multiple. NOT ESTABLISHED: not the one-loop partition function -- the cusp's continuous spectrum is still absent and B739's scattering determinant remains the missing half; and NOT that analytic torsion IS the graviton determinant -- Pfaff computes Ray-Singer analytic torsion, what is identified here is the RUELLE FACTORS, exactly and by definition, and the torsion-to-determinant step is a further identification that is not claimed. Gate 5 untouched: no measured value appears.
